title: Dexcom Time-in-Range Below Target
app: Apple Health / Apple Watch exports, Oura, WHOOP, Dexcom, Levels, LibreView, Eight Sleep, Withings, and Garmin Body Battery feeds via vendor APIs, exports, Home Assistant bridges, and Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=dexcom:egv
| bin _time span=1d
| stats count as samples, count(eval(glucose_value>=70 AND glucose_value<=180)) as in_range by person _time
| eval tir_pct=round(100*in_range/samples,1)
| where samples>0 AND tir_pct<70
| sort tir_pct
description: Uses Dexcom CGM readings telemetry to monitor daily time-in-range performance in index=personal.
value: Splunk turns the feed into an operational check for days when glucose control slipped below target, so the signal does not stay buried inside separate consumer apps or exports.
implementation: Ingest Dexcom CGM readings data through its real API, export, MQTT bridge, or open-source connector into `index=personal`; preserve the fields referenced in the SPL and schedule the search on a daily cadence.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Personal HEC index — HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.
• **Subcategory context**: Health, Sleep & Wearables — typical feeds: Apple Health metrics (`apple:health`), Oura Ring daily readiness/sleep (`oura:daily`), Whoop recovery/strain (`whoop:cycle`), Withings body/blood-pressure (`withings:measure`), Dexcom CGM glucose (`de.
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `dexcom:egv`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Personal HEC index** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=dexcom:egv`.

**Collection method:** HTTP Event Collector token on index=personal.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `POST https://<splunk>:8088/services/collector/event`.

**Suggested poll interval:** depends on upstream connector.

**Key fields to extract:** `sourcetype-specific — see search filters`.

**Typical connector stack:** Apple Health / Apple Watch exports (Health Auto Export, Shortcuts) via HEC; Oura, Whoop, Withings, Dexcom APIs via scripted REST inputs..

**Author notes:** Ingest Dexcom CGM readings data through its real API, export, MQTT bridge, or open-source connector into `index=personal`; preserve the fields referenced in the SPL and schedule the search on a daily cadence.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "dexcom:egv", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=dexcom:egv earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Dexcom Time-in-Range Below Target** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=dexcom:egv`) across the full search range. It applies numeric thresholds on `glucose_value` (>= 70) after count — tune these constants to your household baseline.

**Fields this search depends on:** `_time`, `glucose_value`, `person`, `samples`, `tir_pct`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=dexcom:egv
| bin _time span=1d
| stats count as samples, count(eval(glucose_value>=70 AND glucose_value<=180)) as in_range by person _time
| eval tir_pct=round(100*in_range/samples,1)
| where samples>0 AND tir_pct<70
| sort tir_pct
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Splunk Search → index=personal | stats count by sourcetype. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=dexcom:egv earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table _time, glucose_value, person, samples, tir_pct
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=dexcom:egv earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

**(d) Threshold calibration:** Profile `glucose_value` before alerting:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=dexcom:egv earliest=-30d
| stats perc50(glucose_value) AS p50 perc90(glucose_value) AS p90 perc99(glucose_value) AS p99 max(glucose_value) AS hi
```

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.2.25: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Daily Time-In-Range Percentage Chart (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Personal HEC index — no Personal HEC index events / missing fields:** If `dexcom:egv` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Personal HEC index connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Personal HEC index — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Personal HEC index JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=dexcom:egv | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Personal HEC index — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Personal HEC index — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Personal HEC index APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Bucket misalignment:** `span=1d` buckets on UTC by default — if your routine is local-time based, add `| eval _time=_time + (local_offset)` or use `@d` / `@w` snap.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `1d` buckets.
